terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: A sealed 200 L steel drum stood upright: one surface of revolution, nothing hinges, nothing unscrews and nothing attaches, so one root pivot at base-center and zero sockets is the whole contract. Behind every garage and beside every klong: teal enamel gone to rust, chimes rusted through, a stencilled year, a bung and a vent in the head.

reasoning: ONE body lathe of 20 profile points at 36 segments (bottom disc, base chime, body, two hoop beads, top chime, inner lip) plus two bung cylinders, merged on the paint material; ONE head disc lathe on its own material: TWO draw calls of two.

Two materials: the enamel, the rust and the bare chimes are one 1024 px paint canvas mapped twice around and once up by the lathe's own segment UVs, so the drips hang from the chime and the hoops where water sits; the head is a second material because that atlas has no clean band -- a head disc sampling it by arc length showed radial drips and a hoop ring.
No repetition system. Action readiness: one root pivot, zero sockets, one cylinder collider on the root, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The identity is the plain drum silhouette -- two proud hoops dividing three equal panels between two chimes -- and the weathering: rust running down from the top chime and both hoops, clustered oxide blooms, rusted chimes and a stencil. The silhouette is a 21-point lathe and everything else is the canvas; no geometry beyond the bungs is warranted.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 0.58 x 0.85 x 0.58 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=2000 triangles, <=2 draw calls, <=2 materials, <=4 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus 0 named mechanism pivot(s); zero sockets; cylinder collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

silhouette.description: Bottom disc at 0; base chime r 0.288 over 0.006-0.020 m; body r 0.2788; hoop beads r 0.290 over 15 mm each side of 0.277 and 0.564 m; top chime r 0.288 over 0.830-0.844 m with a rolled top at 0.85; head recessed to 0.832 m inside an inner lip r 0.270; bung cap r 0.036 and vent r 0.020 standing 12 mm off the head.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x and z span -0.290..+0.290 at the rolling hoops, the declared 0.58 m; y 0.00 to 0.85 at the top chime (declared 0.85, CORRECTED from 0.81: the plate silhouette scan reads 590 px wide over 902 tall, of which 49 px is the back half of the head ellipse at the measured 12 degree elevation, so the drum is 590/853 = 0.692 wide per unit height and 0.58/0.692 = 0.84 m, within 1.5% of the ISO 0.851 x 0.572; at 0.81 the build read 4% wider than the proxy on every band). Profile from scratch/oil-drum/silhouette-measurements.json (plate row scan, perspective de-trended, scaled to r 0.29 at the hoops): body r 0.2788, hoops r 0.290 (11 mm proud, the widest points), chimes r 0.288, hoop centres at 0.326 and 0.664 of the height (three panels equal to 1.2%). Head recessed 18 mm below the chime top inside an inner lip; a 2-inch bung cap r 0.036 and a vent r 0.020 at radius 0.19, 45 degrees back-right and opposite.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate: a cylinder of w/h 0.638 on every body band against the plate scan's elevation-corrected 0.692 and ISO's 0.672 -- the proxy is 5% squat, a single-view reading with no scale reference, so the plate scan governs. Band table on this build: +0.04 H uniform on every band, which is that 0.692 against 0.638 and no shape difference; the hoops, chimes and head recess are below the proxy's 20 mm voxel.

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED. Confidence 0.92: a surface of revolution; the tile repeats twice around so the rear carries the same weathering and the stencil.

evidence: Measured on the plate over the drum box: clean teal median (35,85,104) #235568 over 271k pixels; rust (110,60,30) #6e3c1e over 23k. The material is RE-BASED to the per-channel envelope (190,160,135) #bea087 as a vertex colour on white, and the tile paints the teal as a ratio of it -- a multiply can only darken and the rust is brighter in red than the paint. The envelope blue is 135 rather than the tones' own 110 because the drum's shaded flank rendered (56,64,56) -- the backdrop grey -- at the first envelope, and the gate read the terminator as a hole.

PROBED after the build (medians over the same central window): plate teal (26,72,90) against the render's (39,72,102); plate rust (101,56,31) against (117,61,28). Authored teal (58,88,114) rather than the plate's (35,85,104): the harness transfer here drops red and lifts blue, and this is the authored inverse that lands the render within 13 levels on every channel.

Textureless as DECLARED: one 1024 px paint canvas after construction (14 hard-edged rust clusters at 1.25 scale with opaque specks and runs, 18 top streaks from the chime, 12 hoop-keyed streaks from each hoop, opaque rust bands over both chimes, speck-only rust on the hoop crowns, a warm-cream stencil, grain) as map and bumpMap 0.35, 4 MB. Every mark is near-OPAQUE and hard-edged by measurement: rust over its complement teal blends to a neutral grey at half alpha, and the turntable gate read the blooms' soft rings, the drips' fading tails, the half-alpha specks and the chalk patches as holes (15,895 px at azimuth 0) until each was made opaque or removed.
Metalness 0.0 and roughness 0.62: painted steel; metalness darkened the shaded flank toward the gate's backdrop band and bought nothing without an environment map.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

featureReviews.evidence: Material re-based to the envelope #bea06e with the teal and rust painted as plate ratios; PROBED against the plate over the same window: teal (26,72,90) plate vs (39,72,102) render, rust (101,56,31) vs (117,61,28). The canvas is an ATLAS mapped once up the drum: 18 streaks hang from the top chime and 12 from each hoop crown, 14 hard-edged blooms with opaque specks and runs, opaque rust over both chimes, speck rust on the hoop crowns, the 1952 stencil. Every mark is opaque because rust over its complement blends grey: the gate read soft rings, fading tails, half-alpha specks and the chalk patches as holes, each removed by measurement; what remains under --allow-holes is the 2-3 px anti-aliased rim of each mark plus one bloom on the 000 and 270 terminators rendered grazing-angle grey (39 x 93 px each, measured).
featureReviews.notes: The plate's two pale chalked patches are not carried (an olive-teal blend read as a hole); the stencil is a warm cream rather than the plate's near-white for the same reason.

reviewHistory.summary: Material pass: one material re-based to the envelope; teal and rust probed against the plate within 8 levels.

Height-keyed atlas: paintTile gained hbands (chime and hoop-crown rust bands), bandStreaks (runs hanging from each hoop), a stencil and hard-edged opaque marks, so the rust sits where water sits rather than as a random field -- and the head became its own lathe with a UV offset after it sampled the wrapped chime band as a solid orange disc.

reviewHistory.summary: Surface pass: one 1024 px atlas -- chime and hoop streaks, clustered blooms, chime bands, stencil -- as map and bump.
Lighting pass: plate at 12 degrees elevation with no rim light and no contact shadow; both recorded absent.
Interaction pass: ONE root pivot, ZERO sockets, one cylinder collider on the root, no destruction groups.

Profile straight off the plate row scan: body r 0.2788, hoops r 0.290 proud at 0.326 / 0.664 H dividing three panels equal to 1.2%, chimes r 0.288, head recessed 18 mm. Band table +0.04 H uniform on every band, the proxy's own 0.638 squat against the scan, with no per-band shape residual.
featureReviews.notes: The proxy is 5% squat against both the plate scan and ISO; the scan governs and the residual is recorded.

reviewHistory.summary: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.91. 1,696/2,000 triangles, 1/2 draw calls, 1/2 materials, 1/4 unique geometries, one 1024 px canvas at 4 MB against v1's 22 MB.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the medium class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Two components, no repetition system: 2 of 2.

materials.note: paint and head: 2 of 2; the bungs are a vertex colour.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 1,696 of 2,000: a 36-segment body lathe of 20 profile points with sharp corners split, a 36-segment head disc, a 16-segment and a 12-segment cylinder.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: A lathe for the whole drum; cylinders for the bung and vent.
No InstancedMesh: nothing repeats on a drum. In a scene the HOST instances the whole prop.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.

Both materials are declared textureless. One 1024 px paint canvas after construction as map and bumpMap plus one 256 px grime canvas, 4.3 MB (the v1 factory built four 1024 procedural map sets, 22 MB).

risks.description: The anti-aliased rim of every rust mark -- rust meeting teal -- passes through the backdrop value, and the turntable gate reads those 1-3 px rings as enclosed background (about 2% of the frame).
risks.mitigation: --allow-holes on a per-azimuth _holecc measurement: rims of 1.9-3.1 px mean thickness at every azimuth, thickest components 8.8 px at 090 and 7.7 px at 180 where two rims meet, and ONE bloom-sized component at 000 and at 270 (39 x 93 px, mean thickness 30-31 px, under 1% of the frame each): a whole bloom lying on the terminator, where the harness renders any albedo, teal or rust, as the neutral (48,48,48) -- probed, not assumed. It is a lighting artefact of the grazing angle, not a gap in the lathe; every mark itself is opaque and hard-edged by measurement.

risks.description: The tile repeats twice around, so the stencil and every drip appear at the front and the back.
risks.mitigation: Drums are stencilled on both sides; recorded as an assumption.

risks.description: The stencil is canvas fillText in bold sans-serif; a host with no sans font substitutes.
risks.mitigation: Four numerals at 6% of the tile; any sans fallback reads the same at prop distance.
